step/carry: A recurrent network reads a sequence one token at a time, and carries a memory from step to step: the hidden state, h. A subscript t numbers the steps.
step/inputs: Step t takes two things: the memory so far, h of t minus one, and the new input, x of t, the embedding of the current token.
step/mem: W h h mixes the old memory. Its subscript reads h to h: the hidden-to-hidden weights. Here it gives zero point five and minus one.
step/inp: W x h, the input-to-hidden weights, x to h, brings in the input: one and zero.
step/sum: Add the two, and a bias b of minus zero point five and zero point five. That makes the pre-activation, z: one and minus zero point five.
step/tanh: Then tan-aitch squashes each entry to between minus one and one: zero point seven six and minus zero point four six. That is the new memory: h of t is the tan-aitch of W h h times h of t minus one, plus W x h times x of t, plus b.
unroll/unroll: To read a whole sequence, repeat the step. h one comes from h zero and x one, h two from h one and x two, and so on. h zero starts at all zeros.
unroll/same: Every step uses the same three weights: W h h, W x h, and b. Nothing is new per step, so one network reads a sequence of any length.
unroll/memory: And h is all that passes from step to step: everything read so far, squeezed into H numbers.
unroll/shapes: The shapes follow. W h h turns H numbers into H, so it is H by H. W x h turns an input of D numbers into H, so it is H by D. And b has H entries.
